title: YAGNI / Speculative Code Comments
pattern: Comments explaining that a block of unused, dead, or empty code is being kept 'just in case' for future plans.
why_bad: YAGNI violation. Speculative code adds active maintenance cost, requires compilation, complicates search results, and often goes obsolete before ever being activated.
detection: Comments containing future dates or terms like 'will be needed for', 'just in case', 'not used yet', or 'future expansion'.
counterexample: None. Speculative code and its justification comments should be deleted; version control preserves them if ever needed.
fix: Delete the unused code and its speculative comment.
source: Heather Adkins et al., *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* (2020), Chapter 6 ("Eliminate YAGNI Smells"); Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 17 (G9: "Dead Code").
